text: EH-104 Phase B verification: no Docker on workstation so pnpm test:eh104-db and live preflight could not run locally; had to rely on static checks + CI database job wiring. A documented disposable Supabase path or guaranteed CI artifact link would prevent this gate ambiguity.

Repository exploration tools returned stale/truncated file views and Bash treated shell syntax inconsistently; stable line-range reads and POSIX-compatible shell guidance would prevent false inspection results.
openspec status cannot resolve archived changes and lists only active changes without directing callers to the archive path; archive-aware status or a clear hint would avoid a failed lookup.

OpenSpec strict validation rejected a requirement phrased with 'may' despite the surrounding mandatory lifecycle; surfacing SHALL/MUST wording requirements in generated artifact instructions without truncation would prevent the failed validation round.

OpenSpec strict validation rejected a release-governance requirement phrased as 'MAY ... only when' even though it is normative; requiring explicit SHALL/MUST wording in generated guidance would prevent the failed validation round.

Keeping Stage A and Stage B in one OpenSpec change invited premature closure pressure; a dedicated future Stage B change plus deleting accidental empty $env and declaring .papercuts.jsonl as a non-PHI process ledger prevents planning artifacts from being mistaken for release evidence.

Local pgTAP/live-PostgREST verification for the PR1 alias bridge blocked: Docker Desktop not running on this workstation, so supabase db start is unavailable; CI database job remains the executable gate
Bash output referenced no recoverable artifact ID, so the truncated OpenSpec instruction payload could not be read in full; always persist or expose full captured output when fields are truncated.
No TypeScript language server is configured for the project, so exported-symbol references and diagnostics cannot use the required LSP workflow; configure tsserver for src and worker.

ast_edit could not match object properties with a before/after spread pattern when removing repeated allowedSpecimens fields; property-node examples for TypeScript object literals would prevent fallback editing.

A line-anchored insertion into buildInputEvidenceHash landed after JSON.stringify's closing brace because the selected line was not the object tail; block-aware insertion or tighter read context would prevent malformed edits.

A surgical SWAP over the NativeObservation header consumed the export type opener while replacing fields; edit tooling should warn when a replacement range removes a declaration opener but leaves its closing brace.
INS.POST on a destructuring closer placed a new property outside the object pattern; edit tooling should reject property-like insertions immediately after a destructure terminator.

The first EH-111 typecheck exposed expected clean-cutover callsites plus two contract omissions (ResolverDecisionTrace export and narrowed review valueKind); a focused compile after each boundary slice would surface these earlier.

Importing pure normalization helpers from observation-normalization-writer eagerly validates unrelated Supabase/OpenAI environment variables, blocking local policy tests; pure writer payload/input helpers should live in an environment-free module.

EH-106 consumer regression cannot run without unrelated app secrets because its imports trigger environment validation, and the Registry 2.0 corpus failure reports only a generic release-gate assertion without the changed row; test runners need env-free imports and failure diagnostics.
EH-111 runner typecheck found an assertion expression calling a nullable compatibility result inline; focused runner compilation diagnostics correctly identified the unsafe test assertion.

INS.POST on the last imported symbol inserted a new import before the existing from-clause, producing invalid syntax; edit tooling should treat import declarations as atomic blocks for adjacent insertion.

EH-106 consumer regression expected an incompatible provisional definition object to remain exposed; EH-111 correctly nulls the entire non-concrete binding, so the stale assertion obscured the stronger boundary contract.
Final validation passed all functional checks but git diff --check failed on one extra blank line at EOF in observation-read-boundaries.ts; edit operations should normalize a single terminal newline.
Shell on this workstation is not PowerShell: Get-ChildItem/Select-Object fail with command not found. Prefer bash/find/ls or omp tools.
write tool call failed with empty args validation; retry with explicit path+content after verifying existing files.
EH-111 QA checklist used Markdown two-space line breaks, causing git diff --check trailing-whitespace failures; prefer explicit HTML breaks or separate paragraphs in checked-in QA templates.

EH-111 PR #95 merged before GitHub's verify job completed; local checks were green but the remote job failed without diagnostics in the PR summary. Branch protection or pre-merge CI completion would prevent post-merge verification ambiguity.
gh run view --log-failed cannot retrieve a failed job's output while another job in the same workflow run remains active; per-job logs should be available independently to shorten CI diagnosis.

Parallel approval-evidence inspection failed with no diagnostic output when an expected candidate-release documentation path was absent; file-presence checks or per-command errors would make repository investigation actionable.

The skill initializer's generated SKILL.md template did not match the documented TODO skeleton, making a combined patch fail before any requested DB-test files were created; stable templates or explicit post-init contents would prevent this.

EH-111 database contract test could not connect to local Supabase PostgreSQL (LegacyDbConnectError); a running disposable local stack or a documented CI-only invocation is needed before the test can provide execution evidence.
supabase status could not inspect the local stack because the Docker daemon pipe was unavailable on Windows; preflight should report this prerequisite before running database tests.

Rebasing PR #99 onto master produced conflicts across its registry workflow, governed corpus, resolver, and tests; require PRs to stay current with master before archival/closure so database verification uses the real migration baseline.

The eh-117 worktree was 61 commits behind master (5a60d4c vs f87e8fe), so EH-107..EH-116 (migrations 034-041, QA/eh-107..eh-116, test:eh111/112/113/116 scripts) were all missing. Two scouting passes were wasted on the stale tree before the divergence was found. Orca worktrees should be created from, or rebased onto, master when the roadmap item depends on prior items.

next build --turbopack resolved modules from C:/Users/leo because a stray package-lock.json in the home directory made Turbopack infer that as the workspace root. Fixed by pinning turbopack.root in next.config.ts; without the pin the production build fails with 'Cannot resolve @radix-ui/react-select'.

pnpm's default isolated node_modules produces .pnpm paths over 260 chars under C:/Users/leo/orca/workspaces/<long-worktree-name>, which Turbopack cannot read on Windows. Every @radix-ui import failed until reinstalling with --node-linker=hoisted. Shorter worktree directory names or a hoisted linker would prevent this.

pnpm test:eh111 fails at scripts/verify-eh111-clinical-compatibility.ts:184 (unit_dimension_conflict assertion) on an untouched master checkout at f87e8fe. It is a pre-existing red gate that makes it hard to tell whether a new change broke anything.

pnpm build (webpack, without --turbopack) fails with UnhandledSchemeError on node:crypto imported through src/lib/biomarkers/measurement-registry-release.ts -> src/lib/health-systems.ts -> src/components/upload-zone.tsx. The project is turbopack-only, so there is no fallback bundler when turbopack itself is broken.
pnpm typecheck fails after deleting a page under src/app because .next/types/validator.ts keeps a stale import of the removed route. rm -rf .next is required; the error message does not hint at that.
The node_repl MCP kernel is unusable: every js call dies with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for a kernel.js in the OS temp dir, and js_reset does not repair it.

QA/eh-105/ already belongs to roadmap item EH-105 (Registry 2.0 identity cutover, issue #5), but GitHub issue #105 is an unrelated bug. Naming new artifacts eh105_* silently overwrote the existing roadmap QA checklist; only 'git status' showing ' M' instead of '??' caught it. Roadmap ids and GitHub issue numbers share a namespace with no guard.

A new test suite can ship with a package.json script and no CI runner: test:stated-axis and test:stated-axis-db passed locally and CI was green, but neither was in measurement-registry.yml. Same gap as the alias-order-db fixture on #105 - twice in two changes. A check asserting every 'test:*' script appears in a workflow would have caught both.

A prompt can promise evidence the pipeline never captures: extraction.ts told the model a section heading justified emitting a specimen, while the worker wrote section_context as a literal null, so the stated-axis filter discarded every heading-derived specimen. Prompt text and the verification predicate had no shared contract and drifted silently. A check asserting that every evidence channel named in a prompt is actually persisted would have caught it.

openspec flag inconsistency: 'openspec status --change <name>' works but 'openspec validate --change <name>' errors with 'unknown option --change' and expects a positional argument. Aligning validate with the --change flag used by status/instructions/show would have prevented a failed call.

Release governance has two similarly-named hashes with different coverage: digestMeasurementRegistryManifest() covers catalog definitions only, while candidateInputHash covers resolverVersion and gates the seven candidate-release approvals. Checking the first and concluding the approvals survive is an easy and costly mistake. A one-line note in measurement-registry-release.ts naming which hash gates approvals would have prevented it.

pnpm build fails with 'Cannot resolve @radix-ui/react-visually-hidden' from @radix-ui/react-select's own dist; a pnpm hoisting gap in node_modules, unrelated to any source change. Would have been prevented by adding @radix-ui/react-visually-hidden as an explicit dependency or setting a public-hoist-pattern for @radix-ui/*.

openspec instructions <artifact> --change X --json exits 5 and wraps its payload in an error envelope when a schema field (rules) is null; the JSON is still usable but every scripted read has to tolerate a non-zero exit. Emitting rules: [] would have avoided it.
psql and supabase CLIs are unavailable in the Windows workspace, so migration parsing and database smoke tests cannot run locally without Docker tooling.
The TypeScript language server is unavailable, so exported-symbol reference checks must fall back to scoped repository search.
The EH-106 consumer regression cannot start without the repository environment variables; the test should load a documented test env or fail with the required variable names.
The new EH-119 pgTAP command reaches the Supabase CLI but cannot connect because no local Postgres stack is running; QA needs a disposable local database startup step.

Hashline edits with a block-adjacent insertion auto-repaired delimiter balance and left duplicate lines that required a cleanup read and delete; the edit tool should reject ambiguous range boundaries instead.

A hashline replacement anchored at a nearby symbol was rejected after an earlier auto-repair shifted the intended boundary; the edit tool should expose the resolved block or reject before mutating adjacent declarations.
An edit reused an older in-session hash after a prior edit and silently recovered from the snapshot; the tool should require the latest hash or clearly reject stale snapshots.
A later edit again accepted an older hash by recovery instead of requiring a fresh file read; this obscures which snapshot anchors the patch.

Importing normalization-review helpers into the isolated EH-119 regression script pulled server env validation into a pure test and made it fail before assertions; public projection tests should not require deployment secrets.
Local Supabase status could not inspect Docker because the dockerDesktopLinuxEngine pipe is unavailable; the DB migration test cannot run until Docker/Supabase is started.
After changing the EH-119 synthetic review fixture, a range edit dropped its required status field and typecheck caught the mismatch; fixture edits should be narrower or typechecked immediately.
EH-119 pgTAP execution reached Supabase but failed to connect to local Postgres because Docker/Supabase is not running; migration and SQL assertions remain unexecuted locally.

Next build fails before application code with 62 unresolved Radix imports (@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu and @radix-ui/react-select) despite package.json declarations; the workspace dependencies need reinstalling before build/browser smoke verification.
Next 15.5.8 rejects the attempted --webpack build flag, so Turbopack resolution could not be bypassed for smoke verification.
The short git diff comparison used PowerShell redirection and was rejected by the command wrapper; a portable comparison form would avoid shell-specific syntax.

The new EH-119 flow verifier used top-level await for env-gated module loading, but the repository's tsx CommonJS output rejects top-level await; wrap the verifier in an async main or provide an established loader helper.
EH-119 pgTAP execution cannot connect because local Supabase/Postgres is not running; migration and SQL assertions remain unexecuted locally until Docker/Supabase services are available.
The required EH-111 baseline still fails at percentAgainstAbsolute.conflicts missing unit_dimension_conflict; failure predates EH-119 and is recorded as a non-blocking pre-existing regression.

The EH-119 flow verifier asserted action: edit-value inside the form; after moving the API mutation to document-viewer for parent-controlled drafts, the assertion became stale and needed relocation to the API/viewer wiring.

The post-UI-change Next/Turbopack build still cannot resolve declared @radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu and @radix-ui/react-select packages even though package.json and node_modules manifests declare them; typecheck and focused regressions pass, but production build remains blocked by workspace package links.
Next 15.5.8 in this workspace rejects the attempted --webpack build flag, so a webpack fallback cannot be used to separate the Turbopack resolution failure.
The Windows hub launcher could not spawn pnpm directly because it treated the shell command as a non-Win32 executable; UI smoke startup needs the pnpm.cmd wrapper or another Windows executable.

Docker CLI is installed but Docker Desktop Linux engine is unavailable on the Windows host; supabase status cannot inspect the local database, so EH-119 pgTAP and writer-seam execution remain blocked.
The first Supabase readiness check used a duplicated workspace path and failed before running; the check was immediately retried with the correct cwd.

After Docker recovery, EH-119 pgTAP connected but the local database was on a pre-047 schema; the real wrapper signature was missing and the SQL suite ran 0 of 36 planned tests. A local migration update/reset is required before rerunning.

The first non-destructive migration-up attempt reached 047 but failed at the promotion RPC statement; the CLI emitted only a truncated LegacyMigrationApplyError, so the exact Postgres cause needs direct database/migration inspection before rerunning.
The first hashline insertion before the 047 function language clause was rejected because line 205 is a closing delimiter; the edit must use an explicit insertion gap rather than replacing that line.

EH-119 SQL mapping-correction fixture used repeat('g',64), but EH-115 inputEvidenceHash accepts only lowercase hexadecimal; the intended guard test failed on trace validation before reaching the mapping-only rejection.

After reapplying migration 047, supabase test db --local failed before SQL execution because Docker Desktop rejected the Windows QA-Db_tests bind mount with '/run/desktop/mnt/host/c: file exists'; verification needs a direct psql/container fallback or Docker restart.
A surgical replacement of the undo branch dropped the local input declaration and caused a transient TypeScript failure; re-reading the edited range before patching would have prevented it.

Supabase test db on Windows still fails before SQL execution because Docker rejects the bind source /run/desktop/mnt/host/c/... with 'mkdir ... file exists'; a direct psql-in-container fallback is needed for local pgTAP evidence.

The protected review route cannot be browser-smoked locally: Turbopack cannot resolve the declared Radix package links and webpack then rejects a transitive node:crypto import; the public app shell still renders.
The LSP reference lookup has no configured language server for this TypeScript workspace; references must be confirmed from the repository search and existing verifier imports.
The package exposes only the aggregate test:eh119 script, not a separate test:eh119-override alias; the direct command failed before running tests.

A repeat of pnpm test:writer-seam fails before SQL execution because Supabase CLI Docker cannot create the Windows host mount /run/desktop/mnt/host/c/.../supabase/tests; direct docker exec psql remains usable for the same SQL evidence.

pnpm test:eh106 fails before the consumer-cutover verifier when run without the CI placeholder environment; the package does not self-load .env.example, so verification must set four required env vars explicitly.

The prescribed pnpm test:eh111 baseline remains red at verify-eh111-clinical-compatibility.ts:184 because the Neutrophils absolute percent fixture does not report unit_dimension_conflict; EH-119 does not modify that assertion.
git diff --cached --check rejects the repository's Markdown hard-break double spaces in QA/eh-119/checklist.md; trailing-space-free wording is required for the commit check.

EH-121 PR was created with merge conflicts in .papercuts.jsonl, document-viewer.tsx, and observation-review-row.tsx because master advanced after the feature branch; a pre-PR conflict check or automatic branch rebase would have exposed this earlier.

A line-anchored replacement body for proposal.md was encoded with an extra Markdown '- [x]' prefix because edit body rows use a leading '+' delimiter; re-reading the changed range caught the artifact before commit.
The supervised hub watcher could not launch  on Windows (exit 1 before readiness), so PR status must be checked through bounded gh queries instead.
No TypeScript language server configured in session; LSP workflow unavailable for symbol navigation on extract/alias code
The Supabase row probe assumed an updated_at column that does not exist; schema introspection or safer column selection would have prevented the failed read.
Docker-backed SQL verification was unavailable because Docker Desktop's named pipe is not running; a local PostgreSQL/container check would have directly demonstrated JSON null versus SQL NULL.

Line-anchored edit replaced a range one line short and silently duplicated retyped keepers in observation-review-workspace.ts and multilingual-launch-slice.ts; block-aware replacement or a post-edit syntax check would have caught it
verify:registry and several verify scripts import src/lib/env and fail without env vars, but the npm scripts do not pass --env-file=.env; contributors must know to run them with the flag

test:eh111 (verify-eh111-clinical-compatibility.ts:184) and the postgrest revision-embed DB test fail on a clean tree (issue #110), so a full-suite pass cannot be used as a regression signal without prior knowledge

Removing a git worktree that contained a node_modules directory junction deleted node_modules/.bin and part of the real store in the main repo; recovering needed pnpm install --force. Never point a junction at the primary node_modules, or delete the junction with rmdir before removing the worktree
supabase test db --local fails on Windows with 'error while creating mount source path ... mkdir /run/desktop/mnt/host/c: file exists'; pgTAP suites had to be run via docker exec psql instead
The initial biomarker documentation generator write contained an unterminated multiline string and failed before any output; an editor/parser check before execution would have caught it.
A second unterminated fenced-code string remained in the generator after the first repair; a full parse check was needed before generation.
The generator still had a multiline Markdown bullet string near the issue body; the parser caught it before any generated files were written.
Adding the missing alias edit-distance column exposed an earlier malformed function boundary left by a narrow patch; the generator parser caught it before files were regenerated.

Adding the retired-definition expectation replaced the existing analyte count in a narrow line patch, causing generation to report analytes expected undefined; the source contract needed a fresh read before editing.
The verifier count patch replaced its analyte assertion instead of inserting the retired assertion, so the generated count check failed despite the catalog being correct.
The GitHub wiki git endpoint returned Repository not found for Hazyshades/EasyHealth.wiki.git; the wiki must be enabled/initialized before pages can be pushed.
Opening the GitHub wiki through the browser timed out after 30 seconds, so the page could not yet be inspected through the UI.
The authenticated browser relay also timed out opening the GitHub wiki, so interactive wiki initialization is unavailable from the current browser session.
GitHub REST API has no available wiki pages endpoint for this repository; GET repos/Hazyshades/EasyHealth/wiki/pages returned 404.

Toggling has_wiki off and on through the authenticated GitHub API did not create the empty wiki git repository; GitHub still returns Repository not found until the first page is created in the web UI.
The wiki remote remained unavailable after the initialization prompt was acknowledged; GitHub requires the first-page save to occur in the web UI before the remote can be verified.
A follow-up check still found the GitHub wiki git remote missing; the requested first Home page has not been saved in the web UI yet.
OpenSpec instruction JSON was truncated by terminal output, requiring reliance on the visible artifact template fields; expose full artifact instructions through a pageable output path.
An Edit range one line short of the retyped payload triggered auto-repair and left a stale proposal capability line; reject incomplete boundary replacements instead of applying a partial edit.

docs/README.md was readable earlier in this session but the next read returned ENOENT while the worktree reports an untracked docs/README.md; surface concurrent file changes clearly or provide a stable snapshot.
Relative hashline edits targeted the original worktree instead of the dedicated branch; absolute worktree paths are needed when editing a second checkout.
The planning change referenced a phase-0 candidate audit artifact that was not present; create the required reconciliation record before editing candidate files.
The imported observation-read-boundaries module was not found at the expected .ts path; use the repository path inventory before opening route dependencies.
A line-level route import edit overlapped adjacent import blocks and produced a malformed intermediate file; prefer replacing the complete import block when removing grouped imports.

The first Health Profile helper extraction exposed missing route import and nullable observed_at return constraints; compile immediately after moving a typed projection to surface exact boundary types.
The required Registry v2.0.0 documentation-baseline directory did not exist; create the versioned acceptance baseline as part of the documentation change.
The rewritten renderer had a malformed template-string expression; run the target CLI immediately after large renderer edits before proceeding to dependent surfaces.

Renderer migration changed the documentation output API and misunderstood getMeasurementIdentity's tuple input/output; update dependent verifier contracts and use the typed definition object before treating the foundation as complete.
The documentation verifier used unescaped backticks inside regex template literals; construct regexes from escaped string fragments or avoid template literals for Markdown-code assertions.

Exporting the documentation validation helper left its internal callsite on the old function name; use symbol-aware rename or immediately search all local callsites after renaming validation functions.

Technical corpus evidence correctly omitted release data but its explanatory sentence still contained forbidden approval and launchability terms; keep prohibited governance vocabulary out of rendered evidence as well as data fields.
The documentation verifier wrote a nested temporary README before creating its docs directory; temporary filesystem tests must establish the target directory explicitly.
A malformed multiline patch inserted literal patch control text into the verifier; re-read the post-edit file and replace the complete affected tail when an edit response shows escaped patch markers.

The initial Wiki verifier treated all approval vocabulary as forbidden, but canonical alias documentation correctly renders approval metadata; assert export boundaries through its input and effects, not generic content words.
The expected quantitative score-group module path was absent; use the repository path inventory before opening neighboring runtime dependencies.
The explicit Wiki export script receives pnpm's argument separator as a literal '--'; CLI parsing must discard that separator so documented package-script invocation accepts --output.
The documented writer RPC seam fixture path is absent from the working tree; inspect the actual Supabase test inventory before relying on a task's historical path.

The writer RPC seam command connected to a local Supabase database with no public.profiles relation, so direct db tests require an explicit reset/migration bootstrap before their fixture can validate the contract.
A second selector-qualified Supabase SQL read returned ENOENT despite the file inventory; retry the exact path without a line selector before treating a listed Windows path as absent.

The document-review runner fails before its assertions when local required environment variables are unset; the package command should provide safe test defaults or document the CI-placeholder invocation.

The extracted Health Profile input type alone is not enough to call buildHealthProfile: the runtime function also requires a source list, so parity tests must construct both arguments from the route contract.

The new persistence-boundary contract sliced the pipeline block too narrowly and excluded the status assignment; derive the complete mapped insert block instead of relying on an arbitrary character limit.

The acceptance route correctly delegates to acceptExtractedBiomarkers rather than calling the writer directly; contract coverage must follow the service boundary instead of asserting the route owns every writer call.

The reprocess CLI delegates to applyReprocessBatch, while the writer call resides in registry-reprocessing/service.ts; contract coverage must trace the service boundary rather than inspect the command wrapper.
The master SHA's raw URL for scripts/generate-biomarker-docs.ts returned HTTP 404, confirming the documentation generator has not been merged; remote publication must remain gated on the merge.
The current master SHA also returns HTTP 404 for docs/05-data/biomarker-catalog.md, so both the generator and canonical catalog prerequisite are absent from master.
A selector-qualified read of an untracked OpenSpec artifact returned ENOENT despite the change directory existing in the worktree; retry untracked artifacts without selectors.
The numstat-to-jq summary failed because Git emitted warnings and non-tabular diff output on the Windows worktree; use a plain stat or explicitly filter numstat rows.
Git merge-base on this installed version does not support --short; use merge-base followed by rev-parse for abbreviated output.
supabase status timed out while checking the local stack; a bounded non-blocking status command or clearer timeout would prevent the baseline check from hanging.
hub could not launch the Windows npm shim for supabase (CreateProcess error 193); a Windows-aware launcher that resolves .cmd shims would prevent supervised CLI startup failures.
docker ps also hung while Supabase startup was supervised; a bounded Docker health/status probe would avoid blocking database-contract verification.

Registry evidence verification stopped at check:biomarker-docs because generated docs are stale in the current EN/RU/ES worktree; a preflight regeneration or clearer generated-output dependency would avoid an opaque closure failure.

Registry trace verification stopped because the current shell lacks the required Supabase and OpenAI environment variables; a documented deterministic env bootstrap or no-network smoke mode would avoid aborting the complete evidence chain.
The installed  executable is a Python CLI whose  flag means export, not env-file selection; a repo-pinned env runner or explicit invocation syntax would prevent this misleading retry.

Running test:trace-v2 with .env via Python subprocess exceeded the 300-second harness timeout and killed the kernel; a bounded non-network trace fixture or dedicated CI timeout would make this verification deterministic.
Docker version probing timed out after Supabase startup hung; local database and PostgREST suites cannot be proven in this Windows session without a responsive Docker server.
The POSIX-compatible ps helper rejects Windows ps -W flags, so process inspection must use Orca process controls rather than a documented cross-platform command.
The installed OpenSpec CLI rejects the documented validate --change flag and suggests --changes; reading command help is required before artifact validation.
supabase db query --local sends SQL as a prepared statement and rejects multiple semicolon-separated commands; ACL and policy inspection must use one query per invocation.

The approval-bound candidate release check fails after the multilingual corpus changes because approvals.json still carries the previous candidate input hash; the gate output identifies the required owner re-approvals.
pnpm verify:registry fails on the local shell when required placeholder environment variables are absent; the workflow supplies them explicitly, so the command needs the CI-equivalent env to run.
supabase status cannot inspect the local stack because the supabase_db_easyhealth container is absent; database contracts require restarting the local Supabase/Docker runtime.

The English-only editor rule is ignored by the repository, so staging the scoped path without -f makes git add exit non-zero even though other paths are accepted; ignored target artifacts need explicit force staging.

The staged OpenSpec phase-0 audit contains trailing spaces on its date line, so git diff --cached --check rejects the otherwise scoped staging; release artifacts need whitespace-cleaning before commit.

Rebasing the release branch onto current master produced conflicts in package.json, observation-review-workspace.ts, and papercuts.jsonl; the branch was behind the merged EH-119 changes, so manual contract-preserving resolution is required before CI can run.

gh pr create executed Markdown backticks through the Windows shell, attempted to run a repository path, and still created PR #125 with a potentially mangled body; PR text must be inspected and corrected after shell quoting failures.

gh pr checks --watch reports no checks for PR #125 immediately after creation; the pull_request workflow has not materialized a run, so merge readiness cannot be inferred until GitHub schedules or a maintainer reruns CI.
The follow-up papercuts commit also conflicts during rebase because master and the release commit both appended reports; additive JSONL resolution is required before rebase continuation.

After rebasing onto master, the generated biomarker docs drifted because the merged EH-119 catalog/runtime changed the generator inputs; the rebase must regenerate and recommit canonical docs before CI can pass.
GitHub Actions run 31605107655 passed verify and integration but the database job failed; remote failure logs must be inspected before merge, even though the same local database matrix passed.

supabase migration up --local rejects the existing local history because migration 047 is pending before the last recorded migration; the disposable local stack needs --include-all or a clean reset to validate fresh migration ordering.

The full local database matrix reached all SQL suites but the PostgREST cleanup failed because the manually supplied service-role JWT used a user claim instead of role=service_role; rerun with the exact Supabase-generated key before diagnosing the fixture.
A second PostgREST retry still used a hand-copied JWT with the wrong expiration/signature; supabase status -o env provides the authoritative key and the exact-key rerun passed.
gh pr checks --watch again reports no checks immediately after the database-fix push; GitHub has not yet attached the rerun to PR #125, so the branch must be polled through gh run list before merge.

Hashline register copy preserved the proposed approval content but changed its final newline, creating an unintended tracked diff; restore source files after using register transfer and verify scoped names before staging.

PR #126 drifted after release approval: head moved from 3b6ab666 to out-of-scope docs commit 90d2c43, so the required head and approvals-only diff no longer hold; removing it requires an explicitly authorized force-with-lease branch reset.
OpenSpec validate does not accept the documented --change option in this CLI version; --help is needed to discover the supported --changes syntax.

A clean git worktree at registry-v2.0.0-candidate.4 has no node_modules, so pnpm --dir ... check:registry-v2-candidate-corpus cannot find tsx; run the tag checkout's script through the already-installed root toolchain instead.
The planned temporary Wiki publish path did not exist, so the existence check returned a non-zero status before cloning; this is expected setup friction, not a repository failure.

supabase migration list contacted the remote database and initialized the login role instead of staying local; a local-only migration status command would prevent accidental network/deployment side effects during verification
Archived file inventory listed .notes.txt, but the file is absent in the current workspace; deployment context had to be re-derived from live Supabase and OpenSpec state
supabase db query SQL was truncated by nested shell quoting around dollar-quoted text; a file-based or parameterized query path would avoid this inspection failure
git diff --check blocked the commit on a trailing-space-only blank line in the existing registry issue template; pre-commit whitespace validation should identify generated template formatting earlier

After the first EH-121 migration rename, current master also contained migrations 048_resolver_trace_v2_alias_evidence.sql, 049_service_role_data_access.sql, and 050_fix_promotion_rpc_overload_defaults.sql; the release branch needs a latest-master migration scan before choosing the next version.

The documented issue://<owner>/<repo>/<N> form does not support repository-wide listing with a query-only trailing slash; it rejected the URL as an unsafe empty path segment. A documented collection URI example would avoid this failed lookup.
The URL reader percent-encoded an ampersand in the GitHub API query, producing HTTP 422 instead of treating it as a query delimiter. Query encoding guidance needs a working multi-parameter example.

The structural source summary omitted the repeated  path segment for the Health Profile page, leading to a failed read of src/app/profile/page.tsx. Displaying full paths in nested summaries would prevent this ambiguity.

The structural source summary omitted the repeated app path segment for the Health Profile page, leading to a failed read of src/app/profile/page.tsx. Displaying full paths in nested summaries would prevent this ambiguity.

A line-based edit used stale line numbers after inserting worker code and replaced part of reclaimStaleProcessingJobs instead of tick. Re-reading the modified range before the next edit caught the corruption; the edit tool should reject stale positional anchors after a prior edit.

A newly created migration could be written successfully but a subsequent ranged read resolved the selector as part of the Windows filename and returned ENOENT. The reader should consistently parse line selectors for newly created files.

The EH-123 worker import used an explicit .ts extension, but worker/tsconfig.json does not enable allowImportingTsExtensions, causing TS5097. The worker import convention should be documented beside its path-alias setup.
The reader again treated a ranged selector on a Supabase SQL test as part of the Windows filename and returned ENOENT. This prevents targeted SQL review and should be fixed in selector parsing.

Hub could not launch the npm-installed Supabase CLI as a supervised Windows process: CreateProcessW treated the shim as an invalid Win32 application (error 193). Hub needs command-shim resolution or a documented executable path.

Launching Supabase through cmd.exe exits successfully after it backgrounds local services, so Hub cannot observe the configured readiness log. A foreground service mode or readiness command is needed for supervised local Supabase verification.

The local Supabase database was running but had not applied the new EH-123 migration, so the focused pgTAP test failed on a missing table. A pre-test migration-up step in the local test workflow would make this state explicit.

The first EH-123 pgTAP execution exposed that CASE expressions assigning assessment_recalculation_status inferred text rather than the enum. Explicit enum casts in trigger/RPC state transitions would have prevented the migration failure.

EH-123 pgTAP found a PL/pgSQL ambiguity in claim_assessment_recalculation_job: the RETURNS TABLE variable attempts shadowed the job-table column in an UPDATE expression. Qualifying every mutable table column prevents this class of SQL function defect.

EH-123 pgTAP then exposed the same text-versus-enum CASE defect in complete_assessment_recalculation_job. The focused contract isolated the next state transition and prevented a processing job from silently remaining stuck.

supabase test db --local did not retain the EH-123 migrations applied before the prior test, so rerunning the test reverted to a schema without the new tables. The test command needs an explicit migration-up prerequisite or an isolated migration-aware harness.

The local Docker-backed Supabase stack has no psql binary on PATH, preventing non-destructive schema inspection after migration-history inconsistency. Bundling a SQL client or documenting a supported Docker exec probe would avoid reset-or-ask dead ends.

EH-121 regression testing found that EH-123's append-only dependency-event guard blocked the existing controlled lineage-purge cascade. Append-only audit triggers must honor easyhealth.purge_lineage like the upstream EH-121 ledger.

A multi-hunk edit to health-profile-snapshot.ts inserted sort/hash lines at stale positions and corrupted the Promise.all and input pipeline; the tool's delimiter auto-repair did not restore valid code. A full-file rewrite was necessary after re-reading the file.

The pure EH-123 deterministic snapshot test imported health-profile-snapshot.ts, whose Supabase client import validates runtime credentials at module load. Pure canonicalization utilities must live outside the environment-coupled data-access module.

Starting Next.js with only .env.example absent fails in next.config.ts because four required Supabase/AI variables are not documented as a local Docker bootstrap command. The project should provide a safe local env setup path that maps local Supabase status values without exposing secrets.

The supplied Supabase PKCE magic link redirected localhost with access_denied/otp_expired before the authenticated smoke test could start. A fresh single-use link is required; the harness should surface link age and one-time-use state before test setup.

The no-store auth-response edit accidentally removed the existing  declaration, causing Health Profile GET to return 500. A tight insertion hunk obscured the deleted declaration; re-reading and smoke-calling the route caught it immediately.

The no-store auth-response edit accidentally removed the existing profileId session declaration, causing Health Profile GET to return 500. A tight insertion hunk obscured the deleted declaration; re-reading and smoke-calling the route caught it immediately.
The browser wrapper exposes Puppeteer-style page locators but  is unavailable; direct page.evaluate is needed for body text extraction. The wrapper docs should list supported locator methods.
Browser page locator innerText is unavailable; direct page.evaluate is required for body text extraction. Wrapper docs should list supported locator methods.

The line-anchored edit auto-repaired delimiter balance while adding biomarker no-store branches and warned that closing payload lines were duplicated. Re-reading the edited region was required to verify the route remained syntactically intact.

A line-anchored edit used a mistyped script path and silently matched the previously read file by snapshot tag. The edit tool should reject a non-existent filename instead of applying by tag fallback.

The Wiki staging directory did not exist, and the glob tool returned a path-not-found error instead of an empty match. A staging command should create and validate the directory in one documented step.

The package script already includes --write; appending --write through pnpm produced duplicated arguments and the Wiki staging export exited with Usage. The package script should accept an output argument or document the direct tsx invocation.
The requested temporary Wiki checkout path was absent, and glob reported path-not-found rather than an empty result; a checkout helper should create and validate a unique staging path directly.

Publishing the generated Wiki page emitted repeated LF-to-CRLF warnings because the cloned Wiki checkout has platform line-ending normalization. The publish helper should preserve generated line endings without warning.

Final EH-123 pgTAP verification failed before running any assertions because the local Supabase database no longer has the EH-123 assessment_dependency_events table. The test command should enforce or document a migration prerequisite before execution.

supabase migration up --local --include-all tried migration 055 and failed because the local migration history marks 053-054 applied while assessment_recalculation_jobs is absent. The local schema/history is inconsistent; only a database reset can rebuild the missing EH-123 tables.

The dependency probe used require.resolve('@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu/package.json'), but the package blocks that subpath through exports and Node returned ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. Resolve the package entrypoint instead when checking installation.

Combining pnpm install --frozen-lockfile with --lockfile=false made pnpm reject the command as a headless install without a lockfile. Verification should run directly after the already successful frozen install, without conflicting lockfile flags.
Starting the Next smoke server through the pnpm  script passed an extra  as the project directory, so Next tried to open a directory named . Use  for supervised startup.
The supervised Next startup command passed a separator as the project directory; Next tried to open a directory named --port. Use pnpm exec next dev --turbopack --port <port> for supervised startup.

A scoped .env search unexpectedly included adjacent anonymous and service-role key lines in tool output, exposing credentials in the session transcript. Secret inspection must use redacted parsing with no context lines; rotate the exposed Supabase keys before reuse.

supabase migration list --linked could not inspect the production project because this checkout is not linked to a Supabase project. The app points at a remote Supabase URL, but migration status needs a project ref/link or a safe read-only schema probe.
The Node REPL remote schema probe kernel exited before executing because its temporary kernel.js disappeared. Use a local redacted probe or restart the kernel before another remote read.

The browser relay could not attach to the user's localhost:3000 tab and timed out after 30 seconds. Authenticated smoke must use the existing headless session or a fresh link; relay availability is not guaranteed.

supabase migration list --linked --output json emitted human-readable table output, so piping it to jq failed with a parse error. The CLI output flag is ignored for this command; capture the table or use a separate parser.

A second attempt to attach the browser relay to localhost:3000 timed out after 30 seconds, including with a target selector. Authenticated smoke remains unavailable through relay; use the visible tab adoption path or a fresh browser session.
Browser relay also timed out when targeting the EasyHealth page title, so the failure is relay attachment rather than localhost URL matching.
Browser page element handles do not expose DOM getAttribute directly; use page.10532eval or handle.evaluate for attributes. The failed inspection did not alter app state.
The browser run exposes raw Puppeteer page methods, not the documented tab.fill helper; page.fill is unavailable. Use page.click/page.type or page.evaluate instead.

Raw Puppeteer page.click on the onboarding submit button hung until the browser tool 30-second timeout, although typing succeeded; use DOM button.click through page.evaluate and inspect the result separately.

The first remote EH-123 state probe assumed columns from a different migration shape (claimed_at/status/id/input_hash), and PostgREST returned 400 for each query. Re-read the deployed table schemas before querying state.

Receipt rows are keyed by dependency_event_id and do not carry profile_id, so the generic profile-filter probe returned PostgREST 400. Dependency-event absence for the disposable profile is the correct zero-row check.

The cleanup count loop applied profile_id= to the profiles table, which is keyed by id and returned a harmless PostgREST 400; the profile was separately verified absent by id, and all profile-scoped data tables returned zero rows.

Final EH-123 pgTAP verification hit a stale local Supabase schema: assessment_dependency_events was absent, so the test ran zero assertions. The disposable local database must be reset before rerunning migration-backed release checks.

The Wiki export command requires an empty staging directory; rerunning with the existing .tmp/eh123-wiki-staging directory returned Usage and stopped before OpenSpec/build checks. Clear the disposable staging output before export.
The documented bare pr:// listing form rejected a repository-scoped query URL, so repository pull-request discovery required a different route.
No TypeScript language server is configured, preventing symbol-aware references before EH-122 changes; configure tsserver in the workspace for safer cross-file refactors.
The EH-117 review fixture's ALT label is a projected UI fixture, not a resolver-admissible input; policy tests need a resolver fixture sourced from the canonical registry suite.

Inline test fixture inference widened AliasMatchType to string inside a union array; name the fixture with its domain type to preserve the contract.
Expected migration 051 from merged master was absent in the workspace despite merge output; inspect migration numbering before adding EH-122 rather than assuming the documented sequence exists.
Editing package.json failed because the prior-session snapshot hash was stale; an automatic fresh-read retry hint would avoid manually re-reading unchanged context.

EH-122 database contract test ran against a local Supabase database that had not applied new migrations, so the batch tables were absent; provide a disposable migrated test command or migration freshness preflight.

EH-122 database test used the non-existent observation_change_events.source_extracted_biomarker_id instead of the canonical extracted_biomarker_id; schema-oriented test helper would prevent false failures.

A line-anchored batch-service edit landed inside an adjacent object literal instead of the intended query because the source shifted; selector-aware replacement previews would prevent syntactically invalid patches.

Adding the EH-122 verification_reversal writer kind exposed a separate resolution-outcome metric union that did not share the canonical write-kind type; derive both from one type or exhaustively map transitions.

The pure EH-122 service regression test imported the Supabase-backed module and failed before assertions because runtime environment validation ran at import time; isolate pure helpers or bootstrap required test-only environment variables.

A second line-level patch into a multi-argument assertion replaced the message argument with another predicate, producing malformed tests; AST-aware edits or broader construct replacement are needed for repeated call arguments.

The extracted pure aggregate helper intentionally accepts only outcome discriminants, but test fixtures supplied unrelated identifiers and failed typecheck; export a named aggregate-input type or keep fixtures minimal.
A line-anchored edit applied inside handleRetryLoad after the file shifted, so derived batch summary state was scoped incorrectly; selector-aware anchors or a fresh narrow read would prevent it.
A second numeric patch targeted a shifted multiline useMemo expression and corrupted the batch projection block; semantic block replacement should be preferred for nested JSX/TypeScript edits.

The document-review regression command imports runtime env validation but does not load the available local Supabase environment, so it fails before assertions; package scripts should supply a safe test env file or isolate pure tests.
Glob reported .env.example but the file could not be read at the reported workspace path; the repository needs a reliable documented test environment fixture.
Production build failed before EH-122 code because declared Radix UI packages were absent from node_modules after the master merge; dependency installation should be part of workspace provisioning.

The standard Next production build reaches DocumentViewer but fails because it imports observation-normalization-writer, which imports node:crypto into a client bundle; client-safe measurement projection must be separated from the server writer.
A broad import-block edit during the client-safe projection refactor removed adjacent required imports, causing typecheck failures; AST-aware import edits would prevent collateral deletion.
No project formatter executable is installed or exposed through package scripts, so TypeScript formatting cannot be verified mechanically; add a pinned formatter command.

A numeric replacement after inserting a helper overwrote adjacent writer statements rather than the intended calls; edits around shifted control-flow blocks need a fresh local read and whole-expression replacement.
The supervised-process launcher cannot resolve pnpm from the interactive shell PATH; it should inherit the workspace package-manager path or document absolute command use.
The local Next dev server reported ready but returned an empty response for the Documents route, preventing UI smoke verification; readiness should include an HTTP response check.
The OpenSpec apply instructions refer to change-scoped validation, but this CLI rejects --change and suggests --changes; versioned command examples should match the installed CLI.

The documented supervised dev-server argument shape passed a literal -- to Next.js, which it treated as the project directory; process invocation examples need package-manager-specific forwarding syntax.

The Wiki staging-directory existence check reports a generic path-not-found error for the expected absent directory; a dedicated exists-or-empty check would avoid treating normal setup as a tool failure.

git update-index --refresh reported every changed file as needs update and exited non-zero even when generated documentation content matched HEAD; a content-aware status refresh should distinguish real changes from filesystem timestamp/line-ending normalization.
The workspace diff utility rejects the standard --strip-trailing-cr option, so LF/CRLF Wiki parity requires byte-normalization through a separate comparison command.

The local Supabase pgTAP suite failed because Docker Desktop's dockerDesktopLinuxEngine pipe was unavailable after the earlier reset; test runners need a Docker health preflight with actionable restart guidance.

The final production-build rerun supplied only a malformed service-role environment variable, so Next page-data collection failed on missing OPENAI and Supabase public variables; release commands need a validated shared test-env wrapper.
The worktree's .git metadata is a file rather than a directory, so writing a temporary PR body under .git failed; worktree-aware tooling should resolve gitdir paths before selecting temp files.

gh pr checks exits non-zero while all pull-request checks are merely pending, so a bounded wait/status wrapper is needed to distinguish pending from failed CI without treating the initial query as an error.
The CI suite-coverage verifier rejects newly added EH-122 package scripts until the workflow registry is updated; adding a test script must have an explicit CI mapping contract.
